references.text: It resembles the theme of understanding God's actions only afterward, where Jesus says that a servant is not greater than his master, and that the disciples will understand the truth when they have seen it fulfilled.
Jesus' words that he tells things before they happen, so that the disciples may believe when they occur, directly mirror the contrast between present misunderstanding and future recognition in 13:7.
Here Jesus says that he told the disciples about things before they happened, so that when they occur, they may believe, which is a direct parallel to the promise that they will understand afterward.
Jesus acknowledges that the disciples cannot bear all things now, but that the Spirit later will lead them into all truth, reflecting the pattern in 13:7 where understanding comes after the event.
A similar pattern where the disciples first understood the events (here the consecration) only after Jesus was exalted, underscores the theme that truth is revealed afterward.
